title: Passano from London to Francis I, 15 March 1530: ciphered account in Clairambault 331

documents.shelfmark: BnF Clairambault 331, ff. 156r-157v (cipher on f. 157r-v; Gallica canvases f149-f150)

plaintext.source: The diplomatic letter is clear and a related passage was printed by Le Grand, but no decipherment of the enciphered account was found.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF full-resolution images of Clairambault 331, canvases f149-f150
transcription.notes: Provisional sign-level transcription. Curved glyphs are given mnemonic aliases; some lookalikes and a few line-end signs remain uncertain. Clear 'in summa' and amounts are excluded.

system.summary: Undetermined cipher written with a small inventory of letters, numerals, and curved signs in nine account entries; simple one-to-one substitution has failed a controlled test.

diacritics.note: Numerous dots may be letter dots or marks on cipher signs; their function is not established.

system.sibling_key: The 13 March 1530 Joachim cipher on Clairambault 331 f. 149 has a visibly different sign inventory; the Ferrara Passano/Sormano cipher in fr. 3096 was inspected and is also different.
system.notes: The copyist says that a page and three lines of cipher follow. The account has legible scudi amounts and a total but the entries remain unread.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo calls it undeciphered; Le Grand and the Letters and Papers calendar omit the cipher account.

conditions.human_role: The user identified the Gallica target and requested a solve or reading.

solution.what: Located f. 156 and its continuation on f. 157r-v through the Gallica IIIF manifest and downloaded high-resolution images.
Identified Giovan Gioacchino da Passano and compared Le Grand's printed diplomatic letter and Letters and Papers no. 6307; neither prints the account cipher.
Transcribed nine account entries on both sides of f. 157, including 402 proposed cipher signs; separated clear amounts and 'in summa'.
Measured 20 distinct proposed signs and index of coincidence 0.0819; checked repeats and periodic coincidence.
Tried one-to-one Italian permutation search, including a 40 by 80,000-step incremental search, period-specific u/v, French, Spanish, Latin, modern Italian, English, reversal and adjacent swaps.
Tried frequent signs as spaces and as nulls, homophonic mappings, and Italian dictionary segmentation.

A 402-sign artificial Italian monoalphabetic cryptogram of matching entry lengths recovered 20/20 assignments; with 10% and 20% random symbol corruption, 18/20 and 17/20 assignments remained recoverable.
A plain one-sign/one-letter substitution is inadequate for the copied account, or the provisional transcription has more systematic sign conflation than the controls' random errors.

outcome.fraction_read_source: ciphertext.txt: no proposed sign has a verified plaintext value; 0/402 cipher tokens read
outcome.notes: The surrounding clear letter and the account's clear numerals are not counted as decrypted cipher text. No connected cipher reading is defensible yet.
